evidence: The round-0 hunk shows a hand-rolled sendDaemonRequest in the e2e file, and the 6ab780f diff deletes identical copies from both daemon-shutdown.test.ts and the e2e test. The reviewer also said the copies lacked sendOne's settled guard, and the extraction in 6ab780f did not take that part up (see F9).
guidance_note: When a reviewer points at an existing canonical implementation (sendOne), reuse it in the extraction instead of moving the duplicate into a shared helper.

evidence: The original helper registered only data/error/connect handlers, so a frameless close waited out REPLY_BUDGET_MS. 6ab780f added `sock.once("close", ...)`, copying one piece of sendOne's contract by hand without its settled guard, and that is what F9 then flagged.
guidance_note: When matching another function's contract, copy all of it (here close handler plus settled guard plus listener removal) or call it, never one clause at a time.

evidence: spawnDaemonWithEnv(env, sockPath) took the socket path both as an argument and inside env.CC_CANDYBAR_SOCKET. 6ab780f derives it from env and throws if it is unset.
guidance_note: Before adding a parameter, check whether the value is already carried by another argument, and derive it from there if so.

evidence: The new text said "`check` only proves the config parses", while the doc's intro describes parse→merge→validate→register→render and cross-ref validates persist targets. 6ab780f applied the reviewer's suggested wording.
guidance_note: When writing a doc sentence about what a tool does, check it against the same doc's own description of that tool.

evidence: The 6ab780f diff removes a local DaemonHandle interface with the same fields as the exported IsolatedDaemonHandle and imports the exported type instead.
guidance_note: When extracting a function into a shared helper, also delete the local types that described its old return value.

evidence: This duplicates F1: the same copy-pasted sendDaemonRequest, fixed by the same daemon-wire.ts extraction in 6ab780f.
guidance_note: Before writing a second copy of a socket request helper in a new test file, search for the existing one and import it.

evidence: killAndWait registered `once("exit")` with no exitCode/signalCode pre-check, while the shutdown test's own waitForExit had that check. 6ab780f moves waitForExit into daemon-wire.ts and killAndWait now uses it.
guidance_note: When a sibling test file already has a race-guarded helper for the same lifecycle event, reuse it instead of writing a bare listener.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: in 6ab780f the only doc hunk is the `check` sentence near line 715, and the two-tiers paragraph was written in the original PR. The paragraph did imply applyStyle shares "pickers" when its menu has no key. Fixing the doc in 1e5e0a1 was one of the two remedies the reviewer offered, and the reply-hint 'pushback' is wrong because the reply begins 'Plan: valid'.
guidance_note: When a doc claims that a group of controls share a config key, check every member against the config before writing it.

evidence: 6ab780f added a close handler without sendOne's settled guard, and the parallel implementation was the real defect. The race as described is overstated: Node's sock.destroy() emits close on a later tick, after resolve(frame) has run, and rejecting an already-settled promise is a no-op, so the response would not be 'permanently lost'. The agent accepted that race claim unchecked. Replacing the copy with a call to sendOne in 1e5e0a1 was still the right fix.
guidance_note: When a reviewer names a canonical implementation to match (F1 cited sendOne's settled flag, close handler and removeAllListeners), delegate to it in the first fix instead of re-deriving it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 1e5e0a1 only touched docs/interaction-authoring.md and test/helpers/daemon-wire.ts, and the unguarded `find(...)!` in dsl-menus.test.ts comes from the original PR. The sibling test in the hunk guards with `expect(toggleUrl).toBeDefined()` and this one does not.
guidance_note: When writing a test right next to a sibling test, copy its guards along with its setup.

evidence: The flag names 16388c2, which only changed render() retries in the e2e test. The `sock.once("error", reject)` line came from F9's fix (1e5e0a1). Nothing is broken today because sendOne's removeAllListeners cleans it up and a second reject is a no-op, so this is an ownership concern, not a bug. Removing the listener on connect costs one line and is reasonable.
guidance_note: When wrapping a function that takes over a socket, hand off the socket cleanly by removing your own listeners before passing it.

evidence: The 1e5e0a1 diff removes the setTimeout that ran before connect, and sendOne's timer starts only inside the connect callback. A hung connect was bounded before F9's fix and is unbounded after it. The readiness probe makes this rare, but it is a real behavior regression.
guidance_note: When replacing an implementation with a delegate, list each guarantee the old code gave (here: the timeout covers connect) and confirm the new call path keeps every one.

narrative: Round 0 raised seven valid findings, which the agent fixed by extracting test/helpers/daemon-wire.ts. The extraction re-implemented sendOne's close handling by hand instead of calling sendOne, and that drew F9 in round 1. F9's fix delegated to sendOne but dropped the pre-connect timeout and left a wrapper error listener, which drew F11 and F12 in round 4. Every round would still have run for independent reasons (F8 and F10 were original-PR content, and round 4 was triggered by the 16388c2 flake retry), so the cost was extra fix commits rather than extra rounds.
guidance_observations: F1 already named sendOne and its guards, and calling it in the first extraction would have prevented both F9 and F12.
The agent accepted F9's race claim without checking Node's close-emission timing. The fix was still right, but the premise went unexamined.

evidence: The 917ded7 diff shows buildState calling loadConfigOverrides and loadSegmentPaletteOverrides, and each ran loadRawOverrides on the same file. The new loadOverrides reads once and returns both projections. The cost was marginal, but the cleanup was cheap and correct.
guidance_note: When adding a second projection over a file that is already being read, project from the read you already have instead of adding another loader call.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: in 917ded7 the plain `const out ... = {}` accumulator appears as unchanged context, just renamed from loadSegmentPaletteOverrides to projectSegmentPaletteOverrides. The hazard is real, but the agent showed the failure is a silent write-drop, because the __proto__ setter ignores non-objects, not the TypeError the reviewer predicted. The agent also swept the same pattern in applySegmentPaletteOverrides.
guidance_note: When an object's keys come from user config, build it with Object.create(null) from the start, following the existing precedent in src/dsl/render.ts.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 46c4b2e did not touch the e2e test, which came from the original PR and only asserted the status row was unchanged. The reviewer's `not.toBe(before)` would always pass, since `before` was rendered with the drawer closed. The agent compared against `opened` instead and found and fixed a real watcher-reload race in the process.
guidance_note: In an e2e test of a feature, assert the feature's visible effect against a baseline that differs only by the action under test.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 0d55b09 only changed the e2e test, and the switch from loadConfigOverrides to loadRawOverrides in clearConfigOverride is original-PR code. The reviewer conceded it was unreachable, since isValidOverrides empties the file on any invalid key. The claim that `{ ...overrides }` would invoke the __proto__ setter is also false: object spread defines own data properties.

The __proto__ round-trip test was added in F2's fix (46c4b2e) and checked only the segment-palette view, while the nearby coexistence test checks both views. The missing assertion is a low-value but real gap in a test the fix wrote.
guidance_note: When adding a regression test for a key-partitioning edge case, assert every projection the key could leak into, the same way the neighboring partition tests do.

narrative: The rounds raised mostly independent issues against original-PR code: F2 was a relocated accumulator, F3 an original e2e test, and F4 an original clearConfigOverride change. The agent handled each one well: it swept the __proto__ fix into merge.ts, chose a better baseline than the reviewer suggested in F3, and pushed back correctly on F4. The only fix-caused finding is F5, a missing assertion in the regression test written for F2. Fixing F5 is the only reason efb8660 and round 4 happened, since the other round-3 thread was a no-change pushback.
guidance_observations: The agent verified F2's failure mode empirically and corrected the reviewer's TypeError claim, which is the right handling of a confident premise.
F3's fix found a real async-reload race, which shows the value of making e2e assertions observable instead of structural.

evidence: The original comment called the drift 'cosmetic at worst', but primary and accent are not hue-anchored and can mismatch the live bg/fg after a theme switch. The aa25a37 comment states this as a known limitation, which was one of the reviewer's two remedies. The packet does not show whether the promised follow-up ticket was filed.
guidance_note: When documenting a limitation, check each affected case (here, each palette role) instead of describing them all by the mildest one.

evidence: A floating @v1 tag on an action that holds secrets is a real risk, but the reviewer admits the old action floated @v1 too, and the target is the org's own action. The agent explained that install.sh's template generates this file, so the pin belongs in the template. Despite the 'accept' reply-hint, nothing changed in this PR. The packet does not show the promised follow-up being filed.

`params.indexOf("38")` can match a 48;2 component equal to 38. aa25a37 replaced it with a sequential walk that skips 48;2 runs, which is the same skip the PR had already added in segment-interior-color.test.ts.
guidance_note: When the same PR fixes an ANSI-parsing collision in one test helper, apply the same fix to every other SGR parser that PR adds.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: aa25a37 changed only a comment in render.ts and the distinctForegrounds helper, and the GIT_WORKTREE template and its comment are original-PR code. The predicted scoping bug did not occur: the agent's real render showed `(+1 ~3 ?1)`, and Go-style `=` assigns to the variable in its declaring scope. The comment's 'same idiom as $dir' claim was inaccurate, though, so the agent rejected the bug claim, fixed the comment, and added a test for the spacing.
guidance_note: When a comment says new code uses 'the same idiom' as other code, check that the two are actually structured the same way before writing it.

narrative: Round 0 raised a comment understatement, a CI pinning concern, and a fragile test parser. The agent fixed the first and third and correctly declined the pin because the workflow file is template-generated. Round 1's F4 targeted original-PR template code: its bug claim was refuted by a real render, but it caught an inaccurate comment and a missing test. No finding came from an earlier fix.

evidence: The new fgBeforeText parsed truecolor foregrounds without the 48;2 skip that distinctForegrounds in the same file has. The gap repeats cc-candybar#173/F3 and F4's lesson in a new PR, but no fix commit caused it.
guidance_note: Before writing a new SGR-parsing helper in a test file that already has one, build the new helper on the existing parser instead of writing another.

narrative: There was one finding: a new test helper repeated the ANSI parsing gap fixed one PR earlier. The agent went beyond the reviewer's suggestion and extracted a single shared parser, and round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The same unskipped-48;2 parser gap showed up in #173 and again in #175, so a lesson fixed in one PR did not carry over to the next PR's new helper in the same file.
